chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad ibn Abī Naṣr, from Dāwūd ibn Sirḥān, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, concerning:
A man forgot the adhān and the iqāmah until he had entered into the salat (prayer). He said: There is nothing upon him.

key_terms.الْأَذَانَ: the call to prayer made before salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْإِقَامَةَ: the second call immediately before commencing salat (prayer)
key_terms.لَيْسَ عَلَيْهِ شَيْءٌ: no penalty, blame, or required remedy is upon him

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone forgets the adhān and iqāmah until after entering the salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about one who forgets the adhān and iqāmah until he has already entered the salat (prayer). It states that no liability or corrective measure is required of him in such a case.
